title: OmniVia Core Application Contract v1 - engineering memory, continuity and engineering context
description: The engineering-memory extension contracts (SPEC-CORE-ENGMEM-001): continuity session bindings, durable checkpoints and handoff views, engineering preview retrieval over governed records, and the engineering context pack representation. This boundary adds no new authority primitive: observations are proposed governed records created through the existing `memory.create` semantics (record type `engineering.observation`, domain scope `engineering.codebase`), supersession reuses the existing record revision operations, and every result is a bounded view whose authority state is server-owned. Identity, effective grants, workspace and purpose come from the authorised request envelope, never from these payloads. Continuity artefacts are immutable L0 evidence: a stored checkpoint is not accepted knowledge, and a handoff view transfers working context, never permissions or credentials.

EngineeringSchemaVersion.title: EngineeringSchemaVersion
EngineeringSchemaVersion.description: The payload schema version for every engineering-memory payload in this boundary. Independent of the application envelope and workspace format versions.

EngineeringSnapshotRef.title: EngineeringSnapshotRef
EngineeringSnapshotRef.description: A reference to one immutable captured source state within a registered repository. A working-tree snapshot is never asserted to be its base commit, and a branch label is advisory provenance only: it is never a unique identity or an applicability proof.

snapshot_id.description: Identity of the immutable snapshot capture.

repository_id.description: Stable logical repository identity, when known to the caller; the server resolves and validates it against registered bindings.

snapshot_kind.description: Open, bounded code naming how the snapshot was captured, such as `git_commit`, `working_tree` or `source_archive`.

branch_label.description: Advisory display/provenance label; never identity and never applicability authority.

EngineeringRecordVersionRef.title: EngineeringRecordVersionRef
EngineeringRecordVersionRef.description: An exact governed record version: record identity plus exact version. Every engineering relationship, review, priority and citation names endpoints at this granularity; selecting a latest timestamp is never canonical resolution.

content_digest.description: Optional content checksum of the referenced version, when the caller already holds it.

EngineeringApplicabilityStatus.title: EngineeringApplicabilityStatus
EngineeringApplicabilityStatus.description: Open, bounded code naming target-specific applicability of a record version at one snapshot, such as `matched`, `potentially_stale`, `invalid`, `unknown` or `not_evaluated`. This dimension is independent of governance state: an accepted record can remain historically accepted while being unsafe to use at a new snapshot.

EngineeringCoverage.title: EngineeringCoverage
EngineeringCoverage.description: What the serving projections and the applicability barrier actually cover for this response. `projection` names serving-index coverage; `applicability` names whether target freshness work has caught up with the registered source head. Neither is a guarantee of global completeness.

projection.description: Open, bounded code naming projection coverage, such as `current`, `lagging`, `unavailable` or `incomplete`.

applicability.description: Open, bounded code naming applicability-coverage state, such as `current`, `pending` or `unavailable`.

EngineeringOmission.title: EngineeringOmission
EngineeringOmission.description: One bounded statement that content was omitted from a view and why. An omission must not identify an inaccessible record: `field` names the omitted position in this view, never a hidden object's identity or title.

field.description: The position in this view whose content was omitted, such as a section id or a named payload region.

reason.description: Open, bounded code naming why content was omitted, such as `redacted`, `inaccessible`, `budget` or `not_applicable`.

EngineeringSessionState.title: EngineeringSessionState
EngineeringSessionState.description: Open, bounded code naming the operational state of a continuity session binding, such as `active`, `closed`, `expired` or `revoked`. Operational bookkeeping only: closing a session does not mean its external run succeeded, and expiry does not mean the agent died.

ContinuitySessionRegisterInput.title: ContinuitySessionRegisterInput
ContinuitySessionRegisterInput.description: Input for `continuity.session.register`: a trusted adapter or SDK binding one authenticated principal to a service-issued continuity session. Not a model-facing tool: the server derives the principal and effective grants from the authenticated channel, never from these fields. A host session reference is an opaque external correlation value, never an authentication token.

schema_version.description: The engineering payload schema version of this request.

repository_target.description: Optional registered source context the session is bound to.

checkout_hint.description: Optional installation-local checkout hint. An unregistered basename is a label suggestion, never permission to create or write a project.

host_session_ref.description: Optional opaque host-native session correlation value; never an authentication token and never authority.

ContinuitySessionBinding.title: ContinuitySessionBinding
ContinuitySessionBinding.description: The service-issued continuity session binding: operational context, not canonical knowledge. Lease expiry and binding generation fence stale contributors; the binding generation is distinct from the authoritative workspace writer generation, and every write checks both.

principal_id.description: Authenticated principal the binding is issued to; derived by the server, never supplied by the caller.

workspace_id.description: Workspace the session is bound to.

binding_generation.description: Monotonic generation fencing stale contributors against rebind, revocation and takeover.

lease_expires_at.description: When the session lease expires unless refreshed through the trusted adapter.

repository_target.description: Registered source context bound at registration, when one was selected.

ContinuitySessionCloseInput.title: ContinuitySessionCloseInput
ContinuitySessionCloseInput.description: Input for `continuity.session.close`: closes one bound session, optionally committing a final checkpoint in the same atomic metadata transaction. A close without a checkpoint explicitly records that no checkpoint exists; it never fabricates a summary. The expected sequence is a mutation precondition against the session's last acknowledged checkpoint.

expected_sequence.description: Optional mutation precondition: the checkpoint sequence the caller believes is currently the last acknowledged one for this session.

final_checkpoint.description: Optional final checkpoint payload committed atomically with the close.

ContinuitySessionCloseResult.title: ContinuitySessionCloseResult
ContinuitySessionCloseResult.description: Result of `continuity.session.close`. `checkpoint_recorded` is false when the close carried no final checkpoint; that is an explicit statement, never a fabricated summary.

state.description: The session's operational state after the close.

checkpoint_recorded.description: Whether a final checkpoint was committed atomically with this close.

receipt.description: Durable receipt for the final checkpoint, when one was committed.

EngineeringObservationKind.title: EngineeringObservationKind
EngineeringObservationKind.description: Open, bounded code naming what an engineering observation claims to be, such as `finding`, `decision`, `constraint`, `convention`, `bugfix`, `failed_approach`, `hypothesis`, `risk` or `validation_result`. A hypothesis is never eligible for accepted-facts selection.

EngineeringSourceAnchor.title: EngineeringSourceAnchor
EngineeringSourceAnchor.description: One exact evidence anchor: the immutable evidence identity the claim rests on, an optional anchor identity, and an optional source span. A line range alone is not sufficient identity.

evidence_id.description: Identity of the immutable evidence artefact this anchor points at.

anchor_id.description: Optional identity of the anchored span within the evidence.

span.description: Optional exact source span within the evidence.

EngineeringTopicRef.title: EngineeringTopicRef
EngineeringTopicRef.description: A reference to the evolving question or decision an observation belongs to: either an existing topic entity identity or a proposed namespaced topic key scoped by workspace, project/repository domain and sensitivity boundary. Equal keys in different scopes do not merge.

record_id.description: An existing governed record or semantic entity serving as the topic.

proposed_key.description: A proposed namespaced topic key, such as `authentication.session-restoration`. A proposal, never an asserted merge.

EngineeringExternalEffect.title: EngineeringExternalEffect
EngineeringExternalEffect.description: One reported external operation and its reported status. `unknown` is preserved as unknown: reconciling the effect is the owning Runtime's job, and a handoff never retries an unknown effect automatically.

effect_ref.description: External operation reference as reported by the host Runtime.

status.description: Open, bounded code naming the reported outcome, such as `confirmed`, `failed` or `unknown`.

EngineeringContextReceipt.title: EngineeringContextReceipt
EngineeringContextReceipt.description: A reproducibility receipt for the context a checkpoint was produced under: the pack content checksum and its declared inputs. Not a persisted pack handle, and never a bearer token for regeneration.

pack_checksum.description: Content checksum of the engineering context pack this checkpoint references.

EngineeringCheckpointObservation.title: EngineeringCheckpointObservation
EngineeringCheckpointObservation.description: One bounded working statement inside a checkpoint, with its evidence references and an explicit support classification. `claimed` means the agent reported it; only `verified` statements carry validation evidence, and neither classification is accepted knowledge.

evidence_refs.description: Immutable evidence identities supporting the statement, when support exists.

support.description: Open, bounded code naming how the statement is supported, such as `verified` or `claimed`.

EngineeringCheckpointPayload.title: EngineeringCheckpointPayload
EngineeringCheckpointPayload.description: The structured, validated payload of one continuity checkpoint. Preserves working context with unresolved work and uncertainty intact: completed work distinguishes verified evidence from claims, failed approaches and unresolved questions are first-class, and suggested next actions are suggestions only - never permission to execute. The payload is L0 evidence once stored; Core does not become the owner of any plan or external effect it references.

objective.description: Bounded description of the current work, labelled working context.

checkpoint_kind.description: Open, bounded code naming why the checkpoint was taken, such as `periodic`, `before_compaction`, `after_compaction`, `handoff` or `session_close`.

external_run_ref.description: External Runtime/host run reference, when present. A reference, never execution authority.

repository_snapshots.description: Exact snapshots relevant to the work.

accepted_record_refs.description: Accepted exact versions verified by Core at submission.

candidate_record_refs.description: Proposed versions, visibly separate from accepted knowledge.

observations.description: Bounded working statements with evidence references and support classification.

completed_work.description: Reported accomplishments; validation links distinguish verified evidence from claims.

failed_approaches.description: Prior attempts and their evidence, including uncertainty.

unresolved_work.description: Questions, blockers and incomplete investigations, preserved intact.

relevant_sources.description: Source/evidence references rather than absolute paths.

external_effects.description: Reported external operation ids and their reported status, including `unknown`.

next_actions.description: Suggested next actions. Suggestions only; no permission to execute.

context_receipt.description: Optional prior pack checksum and reproducibility inputs.

CheckpointReceipt.title: CheckpointReceipt
CheckpointReceipt.description: The durable receipt a successful checkpoint append returns. Only this receipt proves a checkpoint exists; host hooks and UI claims are not durability guarantees. Replaying the same idempotency key with the exact same request returns this same receipt.

sequence.description: Monotonic checkpoint sequence within the session, assigned transactionally.

content_digest.description: Content checksum of the stored checkpoint evidence.

audit_reference.description: Audit reference for the committed append.

ContinuityCheckpointAppendInput.title: ContinuityCheckpointAppendInput
ContinuityCheckpointAppendInput.description: Input for `continuity.checkpoint.append`: appends one immutable checkpoint to a bound session. The envelope's idempotency key makes a lost-reply retry return the original receipt; reusing the key with a different payload is an explicit conflict. The expected parent sequence serialises competing successors: two clients cannot both become the successor of one checkpoint.

session_id.description: The bound session to append to.

parent_checkpoint_id.description: Exact predecessor checkpoint, required for an explicit continuation.

expected_parent_sequence.description: The parent sequence the caller expects; a concurrent successor makes this append a precondition failure rather than a silent replacement.

payload.description: The validated checkpoint payload stored as immutable L0 evidence.

receipt.description: The durable receipt proving the checkpoint exists.

ContinuityHandoffReadInput.title: ContinuityHandoffReadInput
ContinuityHandoffReadInput.description: Input for `continuity.handoff.read`: reads a bounded, authorised handoff view of one checkpoint. Select the checkpoint exactly (by id, or by session plus sequence); the optional target snapshot lets the view state applicability for the snapshot the receiving agent actually targets. Handoff does not transfer the sender's grants, credentials, leases or approvals to act.

session_id.description: Session identity, when selecting by session plus sequence.

sequence.description: Checkpoint sequence within the session, when selecting by session plus sequence.

target_snapshot.description: The snapshot the receiving agent targets, for applicability framing.

HandoffView.title: HandoffView
HandoffView.description: A bounded, authorised view of one checkpoint for a receiving agent. A redacted view is labelled as a derived view; its own digest identifies the view, never the original artefact. Omissions are recorded without exposing inaccessible evidence identities. Working context here is context, not instruction, and confers no authority.

checkpoint_id.description: Identity of the checkpoint this view renders.

content_digest.description: Content checksum of this view's own bytes; the original checkpoint's digest remains the identity of the original artefact.

redacted.description: Whether this view is a redacted derived view.

objective.description: The checkpoint's bounded objective, as working context.

applicability.description: Applicability of the checkpoint's evidence at the requested target snapshot, or `not_evaluated` when no target was requested.

unresolved_work.description: Unresolved questions preserved intact from the checkpoint.

next_actions.description: Suggested next actions. Suggestions only; no permission to execute.

omissions.description: What this view omits and why, without exposing inaccessible identities.

EngineeringSearchView.title: EngineeringSearchView
EngineeringSearchView.description: Open, bounded code naming which knowledge partition a search reads, such as `accepted` (the default), `candidates`, `working_context` or `history`. Other views are explicit opt-ins behind their capabilities; a multi-view response partitions results rather than interleaving them without labels.

EngineeringPreview.title: EngineeringPreview
EngineeringPreview.description: One bounded preview in an engineering search result: exact record/evidence identity, a truncated bounded preview, and the server-owned authority/applicability facts a caller needs before expanding. Carries no full content, no raw local paths, and never identity-bearing fields for inaccessible objects.

record_id.description: Governed record identity of the previewed version.

content_digest.description: Content checksum of the exact record version, when exposed to this caller.

preview.description: Bounded preview text; never the full body.

truncated.description: Whether the preview text was cut before the record's natural end.

observation_kind.description: The observation kind, when the record is an engineering observation.

governance_state.description: Server-owned governance state of this exact version, such as `proposed`, `accepted`, `contested` or `superseded`.

assertion_basis.description: Open, bounded code naming what the claim rests on, such as `observed`, `derived`, `reported` or `hypothesis`.

topic_key.description: The scoped topic key, when the record belongs to a topic.

repository_id.description: Repository the record's applicability claims, when any.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the record's applicability claims, when any.

applicability.description: Target-specific applicability of this version, or `not_evaluated` when no target was in scope.

review_due.description: Whether the version's review schedule marks it due. A due flag is not proof of falsity.

evidence_available.description: Whether the record's evidence is available to this caller under current authorisation.

EngineeringSearchInput.title: EngineeringSearchInput
EngineeringSearchInput.description: Input for `engineering.search`: bounded preview retrieval over the authorised engineering frontier. The view defaults to `accepted`; every other view is an explicit opt-in behind its capability. The repository target, when given, scopes retrieval to one registered snapshot. Authorisation, projection freshness and applicability eligibility are applied before scoring; a bounded response never presents a truncated pre-authorisation top-k as complete.

view.description: Which knowledge partition to read; defaults to `accepted`.

repository_target.description: Optional registered snapshot the search is scoped to.

limit.description: Maximum previews to return; the service default is 20 and the hard maximum 100.

page.description: Opaque continuation position. A changed authority epoch, projection snapshot or bound scope invalidates the token with an explicit restart response.

EngineeringSearchResult.title: EngineeringSearchResult
EngineeringSearchResult.description: Result of `engineering.search`: one page of bounded previews plus the coverage facts that qualify them.

previews.description: The authorised previews on this page.

page.description: The pagination position this read reached; `{}` means the read is exhausted.

coverage.description: Projection and applicability coverage qualifying this page.

EngineeringRelationEdge.title: EngineeringRelationEdge
EngineeringRelationEdge.description: One relationship candidate between two exact record versions. Relation vocabulary is open (`related`, `compatible`, `scoped_difference`, `conflicts_with`, `supersedes`, `not_conflict`); state is independent (`pending`, `assessed`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `obsolete`). A pending or rejected edge is visible as a candidate, never as governed truth, and a `not_conflict` verdict is not evidence that either endpoint is correct.

EngineeringExpandInput.title: EngineeringExpandInput
EngineeringExpandInput.description: Input for `engineering.expand`: bounded expansion from one authorised anchor into surrounding history, relations and evidence references. Expansion obeys its own depth, node and edge budgets, and never traverses through a hidden node to reveal another relationship.

anchor.description: The exact authorised record version to expand from.

depth.description: Expansion depth; the service default is 1 and the hard engineering cap 3.

node_limit.description: Maximum nodes returned; the service default is 30 and the hard engineering cap 200.

edge_limit.description: Maximum edges returned; the service default is 60 and the hard engineering cap 400.

EngineeringExpandResult.title: EngineeringExpandResult
EngineeringExpandResult.description: Result of `engineering.expand`: bounded nodes and filtered edges around the anchor, with explicit truncation and coverage.

nodes.description: Exact record versions reached, including the anchor.

edges.description: Relationship candidates whose endpoints are both visible to this caller.

truncated.description: Whether expansion stopped at a budget rather than exhausting the neighbourhood.

coverage.description: Projection and applicability coverage qualifying this expansion.

EngineeringBudget.title: EngineeringBudget
EngineeringBudget.description: Caller-requested bounded budgets for one engineering context build. Byte and token limits are simultaneous limits, not conversions of one another. Effective budgets are the minimum of the request, the granted profile and server hard limits; zero, negative, non-finite, oversized or inconsistent values are rejected.

model_tokens.description: Maximum model-facing tokens for the complete rendering; the proposed default is 4000 and the hard ceiling 16000.

model_bytes.description: Maximum model-facing UTF-8 bytes for the complete rendering; the proposed default is 16384 and the hard ceiling 65536.

hydrations.description: Maximum full source hydrations for the build; the proposed default is 8 and the hard ceiling 32.

evidence_bytes.description: Maximum total evidence bytes read for the build; the proposed default is 262144 and the hard ceiling 1048576.

EngineeringCitation.title: EngineeringCitation
EngineeringCitation.description: One deterministic internal citation inside a pack: a resolvable reference to the exact record version and/or evidence the cited content came from. Citation ids are internal references, not self-referential pack URLs, and following one always requires fresh authorisation.

citation_id.description: Deterministic citation identity within this pack.

record_ref.description: The exact record version cited, when the citation names a record.

evidence_id.description: The immutable evidence identity cited, when the citation names evidence.

EngineeringConflictNotice.title: EngineeringConflictNotice
EngineeringConflictNotice.description: A notice that two or more eligible, visible assertions materially conflict. The group is atomic: the pack never silently chooses the most recent or most repeated claim as truth. When the conflicting conclusions cannot fit, the notice stands alone and the unsafe conclusion is omitted.

records.description: The conflicting record versions, all visible to this caller.

status.description: Open, bounded code naming the conflict state, such as `unresolved`, `resolved` or `scoped_difference`.

note.description: Bounded explanatory note permitted for this caller.

EngineeringPackSection.title: EngineeringPackSection
EngineeringPackSection.description: One section of an engineering context pack, carrying its exact content, its citations, and one explicit knowledge partition. The partition is the integrity contract: candidate assertions never appear under `accepted_knowledge`, and working context is never an instruction or grant.

section_id.description: Unique section identity within this pack.

kind.description: Open, bounded code naming the section's rendering kind, such as `decision_summary`, `evidence_excerpt` or `working_context`.

partition.description: Open, bounded code naming the knowledge partition, exactly one of `accepted_knowledge`, `source_evidence`, `candidate_findings`, `working_context` or `history`.

content.description: The section's exact content as it enters the model-facing rendering.

citation_ids.description: Citations resolving this section's claims; a substantive section has at least one.

EngineeringRendering.title: EngineeringRendering
EngineeringRendering.description: The complete model-facing rendering of a pack: one canonical UTF-8 string containing section labels, content, authority/applicability warnings and compact citations, counted exactly with the pinned tokenizer. Headers, citation labels, warnings and separators count when they are sent to the model; transport metadata that is not sent is separately byte-capped and lives elsewhere.

renderer_version.description: Version of the renderer that produced this text.

token_count.description: Exact token count of `text` under the pinned supported tokenizer.

EngineeringBudgetOutcome.title: EngineeringBudgetOutcome
EngineeringBudgetOutcome.description: The budget as requested, as effectively applied, and as actually consumed by this build. Actual source-read bytes and hydration counts are reported, so a pack cannot exceed its caps invisibly.

requested.description: What the caller requested, when the caller stated a budget.

effective.description: The minimum of request, granted profile and server hard limits actually applied.

source_bytes_read.description: Total evidence bytes actually read during the build.

EngineeringTargetApplicability.title: EngineeringTargetApplicability
EngineeringTargetApplicability.description: One target snapshot's applicability statement inside a pack, so a consumer can see which target each applicability claim belongs to.

snapshot.description: The target snapshot this statement is about.

status.description: Applicability of the pack's records at this target, evaluated at the pinned BuildContext.

EngineeringContextPack.title: EngineeringContextPack
EngineeringContextPack.description: The engineering context pack representation (`format_version` `engineering_context.v1`): a non-persisted deterministic view built from a pinned BuildContext and the authorised frontier. `pack_id` equals the canonical artifact checksum computed after removing exactly the root `pack_id` and the nested reproducibility artifact checksum. A checksum is not a bearer token: following any citation requires fresh authorisation, and a previously generated pack may no longer be deliverable after revocation even when its bytes are reproducible.

format_version.description: The engineering pack representation format. This representation is never decoded as a legacy application-v1 ContextPackBuildResult.

pack_id.description: The pack's content identity: SHA-256 of the canonical result after removing exactly root `pack_id` and nested `reproducibility.artifact_checksum`.

normalized_request.description: The normalized build request the pack answers.

targets.description: The exact snapshots this pack is about.

profile.description: The retrieval profile used, such as `investigate`, `implement`, `review` or `resume`. A retrieval template, not a permission or work instruction.

sections.description: The pack's sections, each under exactly one knowledge partition.

conflicts.description: Mandatory conflict notices; reserved before optional content is selected.

uncertainties.description: Mandatory uncertainty notices, reserved before optional content is selected.

omissions.description: What was omitted and why, without exposing inaccessible identities.

rendering.description: The complete model-facing rendering and its exact counts.

budget.description: Requested, effective and actually consumed budgets.

applicability.description: Per-target applicability, evaluated at the pinned BuildContext.

authorization_context.description: The authorisation facts (epochs, policy digests) this pack was built under. Historical authorisation is not permission to disclose today.

reproducibility.description: Evaluation time, source/record versions, projection versions and watermarks, renderer/tokenizer versions, ranking profile, frontier checksum, policy/ACL epoch and resolver version, plus the artifact canonicalisation and checksum. Replay requires all of these inputs; missing inputs mean a new build gets a new identity.

fresh_authorization_required.description: Always true: consuming this pack always requires a fresh authorisation check.

EngineeringContextBuildInput.title: EngineeringContextBuildInput
EngineeringContextBuildInput.description: Input for `engineering.context.build`: builds one non-persisted engineering context pack against explicit repository snapshot targets. Workspace, principal, purpose and grants remain in the envelope. The request carries no free-form system prompt, arbitrary model instruction, raw SQL, server filesystem path, new authority field or synchronous summarisation-provider setting; historical diagnosis is an explicit separate request type or capability, never an automatic fallback.

query.description: The bounded retrieval intent for this build.

targets.description: Explicit repository snapshot targets for this pack.

profile.description: Retrieval profile: one of `investigate`, `implement`, `review` or `resume`. A retrieval template, not a permission or work instruction.

topic_refs.description: Optional topics to centre the pack on.

checkpoint_refs.description: Optional authorised checkpoint identities whose working context may enter the pack.

budget.description: Optional caller-requested budgets; effective budgets are also bounded by the granted profile and server hard limits.

EngineeringContextBuildResult.title: EngineeringContextBuildResult
EngineeringContextBuildResult.description: Result of `engineering.context.build`. Nothing is persisted: the pack is regenerated or fails with an explicit replay-inputs error, never silently reissued from absent projections.

pack.description: The built pack. Non-persisted; regeneration requires its recorded replay inputs.

ContextPrioritySetInput.title: ContextPrioritySetInput
ContextPrioritySetInput.description: Input for `context.priority.set`: one principal's own selection preference for one exact visible record version. Priority is `normal` or `preferred`; it can influence selection only after authorisation and applicability checks, never changes governed record versions, approval state or evidence confidence, and a pin count never becomes an evidence-confidence input.

target.description: The exact visible record version the preference applies to.
The record version the preference now applies to.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the preference, when one was set.

audit_reference.description: Audit reference for the audited preference change.

EngineeringReviewRecordInput.title: EngineeringReviewRecordInput
EngineeringReviewRecordInput.description: Input for `engineering.review.record`: records one review or deterministic-validation attestation for one exact record version at one target snapshot. This cannot accept knowledge, cannot clear a stale or unknown target applicability without new evidence, and never replaces the governed review path.

record_ref.description: The exact record version being reviewed.

target_snapshot.description: The target snapshot the review is recorded against.

review_outcome.description: Open, bounded code naming what the review recorded, such as `acknowledged`, `evidence_attached` or `revision_proposed`.

review_evidence_id.description: Immutable evidence identity backing the review, when evidence was attached.

expected_assessment_version.description: Mutation precondition: the applicability assessment version the caller believes is current.

EngineeringReviewRecordResult.title: EngineeringReviewRecordResult
EngineeringReviewRecordResult.description: Result of `engineering.review.record`. The returned applicability is the target-specific assessment after this review; acknowledging review without sufficient evidence leaves `potentially_stale`, `invalid` and `unknown` intact.

applicability.description: The target-specific assessment after this review.

revision_ref.description: The proposed revision created by this review, when the outcome proposed one.

audit_reference.description: Audit reference for the recorded attestation.
